post.description: Public. Emails a 6-digit code and a magic link (15 minutes, single use) to the address. Always answers 200 `{sent: true, retry_after}` whether or not the address has an account; for `intent=signin` with no account the email offers sign-up instead. Within 30 seconds of the previous email for the same address and intent no new email is sent and `retry_after` is the remaining wait. Rate-limited per client IP and per email address (429 `rate_limited` with Retry-After).

post.description: Public. Checks the 6-digit code of the latest sign-in email sent to the address and consumes it. The user is found or, on first sign-in, created, and the address is marked verified. Answers the session bundle (`amr: ["email"]`; `remember` picks the session lifetime) or, when the user has two-factor authentication enabled, `{status: "2fa_required", pre_auth_token}`. Either answer carries the `next` path the email was requested with; a new user who requested none gets `/onboarding/about`. A wrong code, an unknown address and an address with no outstanding email all answer `invalid_code`; the fifth wrong code locks the email (`too_many_attempts`) until a new one is requested. Rate-limited per email address (429 `rate_limited` with Retry-After).

post.description: Public; called by the UI's server side with the token of a magic link it was opened with. Checks the token and consumes the email, so the link (and its code) work once. The user is found or, on first sign-in, created, and the address is marked verified. Answers the session bundle (`amr: ["email"]`; `remember` picks the session lifetime) or, when the user has two-factor authentication enabled, `{status: "2fa_required", pre_auth_token}`. Either answer carries the `next` path the email was requested with. An unknown, used or superseded link answers `invalid_token`; an expired one `code_expired`.

get.description: Public browser navigation; the provider redirects here. Takes the sign-in state (single use), exchanges the code with the PKCE verifier and reads a verified email: Google from the `id_token` (signature, audience, nonce and `email_verified` checked), GitHub from the primary verified address of `/user/emails`. The user is matched by (provider, subject), then by verified email (the identity is linked), else created. The session bundle (`amr: [provider]`), or the `2fa_required` answer when the user has two-factor authentication, is kept for 60 seconds under a one-time code and the browser is redirected (302) to `{public_ui_url}/auth/callback?code=…`, whose server side redeems it; tokens never appear in a URL. Failures redirect to `{public_ui_url}/sign-in?error=<code>`: `oauth_state_mismatch` (unknown, expired, used or foreign state; rejected code or PKCE verifier; wrong nonce), `oauth_email_unverified` (no verified email), `oauth_denied` (consent declined), `account_deleting`, `invalid_request` or `internal_error`. A provider that is not configured answers 404.

post.description: Public. Verifies the authenticator's assertion for the options of `challenge_id`, resolving the user from the passkey's user handle, and answers the session bundle (`amr: ["passkey"]`; `remember` picks the session lifetime) with `next` echoed. A passkey is phishing-resistant and user-verifying, so two-factor authentication is not asked for. Answers 401 `passkey_unknown` for a passkey that is not registered, and 401 `passkey_failed` when the challenge is unknown, expired or used, the assertion does not verify, or its signature counter went backwards (a possibly cloned authenticator). Rate-limited per IP (429 `rate_limited` with Retry-After).

Verifies the authenticator's response to the options of `challenge_id` and stores the passkey. Without `name` it is named after the authenticator (or the browser and OS). Answers 401 `passkey_failed` when the challenge is unknown, expired or used, or the response does not verify, and 409 `passkey_already_registered` for a credential that is already registered. Audited as `passkey.added`; the user is emailed a security alert.
